Settings.Global.DEVELOPMENT_SETTINGS_ENABLED reports whether developer options are enabled.
Enabled provides diagnostic context; it does not mean root access, CPU saturation or a compromised phone.
Security settings can change the operating context of the agent and other apps. They are not a performance score or an automatic compliance verdict.
If a setting changes during a session, use the recorded time to compare nearby errors. A matching time is a clue, not proof of a cause.

Counts packages returned for the current user by PackageManager or separately by Knox ApplicationPolicy.
A count of 100 is inventory size, not 100 running processes. Visibility restrictions can reduce the count.
Inventory changes can identify installations or upgrades near a performance change. Package count does not measure active workload.
An added package appears in the next snapshot and the change list. Removal is reported only when both compared lists have full visibility.
Counts visible installed packages with ApplicationInfo.FLAG_SYSTEM.
System packages may be disabled or updated. This flag is not evidence of current CPU or memory consumption.

ConnectivityManager reports the transport of the default app-visible network: Wi-Fi, cellular, Ethernet, VPN, other or none.
A switch from Wi-Fi to cellular may coincide with latency or cost changes. This field does not measure throughput.
Network state can affect upload delays, retries and power consumption. A snapshot cannot identify the cause of packet loss or slow requests.
Compare the timestamp of a network switch with upload retries. A default network can be present while the server is unreachable.
True when ConnectivityManager exposes capabilities for a default network.
A present network can lack Internet access or require a captive portal. This is not a successful backend connectivity test.

ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED reports the hardware health category.
Overheat or overvoltage merits correlation with temperature and charging. Good is not a measured percentage of remaining battery life.
Charging and power conditions can affect thermal behavior, battery drain and background scheduling. Interpret readings together, not as universal thresholds.
Compare readings before and after connecting a charger, allowing for the sampling interval. A single sample can miss a short transition.
ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED reports charging, discharging, not charging or full.
A connected charger may coexist with not charging, for example at a thermal limit. State alone does not identify the reason.
Charging and power conditions can affect thermal behavior, battery drain and background scheduling. Interpret readings together, not as universal thresholds.
Compare readings before and after connecting a charger, allowing for the sampling interval. A single sample can miss a short transition.
Battery broadcast voltage in millivolts is converted to volts.
For example, 4000 mV is 4 V. Compare with charge state and device specifications; voltage alone is not battery capacity.
Charging and power conditions can affect thermal behavior, battery drain and background scheduling. Interpret readings together, not as universal thresholds.
Compare readings before and after connecting a charger, allowing for the sampling interval. A single sample can miss a short transition.
BATTERY_PROPERTY_CURRENT_NOW is converted from microamps to milliamps.
Android defines positive as net charging and negative as discharging. Vendor behavior can vary; correlate the sign with charge state. This is a snapshot, not an interval average.
Charging and power conditions can affect thermal behavior, battery drain and background scheduling. Interpret readings together, not as universal thresholds.
Compare readings before and after connecting a charger, allowing for the sampling interval. A single sample can miss a short transition.
BATTERY_PROPERTY_CHARGE_COUNTER is converted from microamp-hours to milliamp-hours.
2000000 µAh becomes 2000 mAh. This is remaining charge, not design capacity or a direct battery-health score.
Charging and power conditions can affect thermal behavior, battery drain and background scheduling. Interpret readings together, not as universal thresholds.
Compare readings before and after connecting a charger, allowing for the sampling interval. A single sample can miss a short transition.
PowerManager.isPowerSaveMode reports the Android power-saving mode.
The mode can affect scheduling and background behavior. A true value does not prove that a specific delay was caused by it.
Charging and power conditions can affect thermal behavior, battery drain and background scheduling. Interpret readings together, not as universal thresholds.
Compare readings before and after connecting a charger, allowing for the sampling interval. A single sample can miss a short transition.
Process.getElapsedCpuTime returns CPU milliseconds consumed by this process.
It grows across all agent threads and resets with the process. CPU time can grow faster than wall time on multiple cores.
Agent resource readings help estimate monitoring overhead. Their changes may reflect collection, database work or graph rendering; they do not represent every app on the device.
Compare the same workload with OEM collection enabled and disabled. Ignore rate values until a second sample after startup or a pause establishes a baseline.
Difference between successive process CPU-time samples in a continuous OEM resource segment.
120 ms over a 60 s sample interval means 120 ms of agent CPU work. The first sample and the first after a pause have no delta.
Agent resource readings help estimate monitoring overhead. Their changes may reflect collection, database work or graph rendering; they do not represent every app on the device.
Compare the same workload with OEM collection enabled and disabled. Ignore rate values until a second sample after startup or a pause establishes a baseline.
100 times the process CPU-time delta divided by the monotonic elapsed-time delta.
120 ms over 60000 ms gives 0.2 percent. 100 percent is one fully occupied core; parallel threads can exceed 100. This is not system CPU utilization.

Shared pages are proportionally attributed. 1024 KiB becomes 1048576 bytes. PSS is not RSS and is not total device RAM usage.

Android camera-disabled policy and Knox camera-enabled policy are read separately.
An allowed policy does not grant this APK camera permission or prove that a camera exists. No images are accessed.
Restrictions can explain why a feature is unavailable despite compatible hardware. The agent only reads policy; no setting, password, package or device state is changed.
If Android and Knox disagree, check the source and scope: permission to configure Wi-Fi differs from permission to use it. No restriction is not a guarantee that a feature works.
Android reports the user restriction on USB file transfer; Knox reports whether USB host storage is allowed.
These are different operations and scopes. Compare each source independently; an allowed state is not evidence of a connected USB disk.
